target_customer: Enterprises and software companies that need continuous vulnerability discovery and patching in their codebases
problem: Security teams cannot find and fix vulnerabilities as fast as code ships and attackers use AI. NebuSec pitches an AI agent (VEGA) that finds bugs, proves them and proposes patches.
business_model: B2B software subscription for code security, plus security audits and incident response services
product_category: AI application security and vulnerability research

founders.name: Eten Zou
founders.background_notes: Automated vulnerability research, Pwn2Own winner per the launch post, spoke at USENIX Security and NDSS.

founders.name: Yuan Tan
founders.background_notes: DARPA funded program analysis research, Black Hat USA speaker.

founders.name: Frank Wu
founders.background_notes: Member of r3kapig CTF team, DEF CON finalist, led a DARPA AIxCC automated program repair team.

founders.name: Xiaochuan Yu
founders.background_notes: DEF CON finalist three years running, over $200K in Chrome bug bounties, core member of r3kapig.

competitors.name: XBOW
competitors.traction_then: Topped the HackerOne leaderboard and published results of 1,060 autonomous attacks in a March 2026 post
competitors.funding_then: Reported Series C in March 2026, amount reported differently by sources ($120M or $155M)

competitors.name: RunSybil
competitors.what: AI native platform running continuous autonomous pentests against live applications
competitors.funding_then: Reported $40M raise in 2026 by one outlet

technical_complexity.rationale: Finding real zero days autonomously with an AI agent is research grade. The team's CTF and DARPA AIxCC background is the enabler, and the claims of kernel and browser exploits are self reported.

defensibility.rationale: Elite vulnerability research talent is scarce and hard to copy, and a published CVE record builds credibility. Models improve fast for everyone, which limits any tooling moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well funded AI pentest startups and big security vendors were already building the same wedge in early 2026. No acquisition or copy of NebuSec found so far.

market_need_then: AI lowers the cost of attacks and code volume is rising, so demand for automated vulnerability discovery and fixing is high. The company claims about $580K in Google VRP bounties and over 238 CVEs, all self reported.

branding.domain_note: Uses nebusec.ai. YC lists the company as Nebula Security while the domain and GitHub use NebuSec.

identity.logo: Not described in any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and credential led, for example founded by the world's number one hacking team

branding.brand_signature: The Audited by NebuSec mark, meant as a credibility signal for audited products
branding.community_and_virality: Named exploits (IonStack, GhostLock, nginx-poolslip) are published as research and talks at Black Hat and DEF CON, but no merch or fan community was found.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong credibility signalling through named research, but the brand is new and confusable with the similar names Nebulock and Nebula Security, and only self published material was found.

outcome_analysis: NebuSec is a very young Summer 2026 company with a team of unusually credentialed vulnerability researchers, and its story rests on founder market fit and a timing tailwind from AI driven security. It is Active, with no exit. The key risks are heavy competition from well funded AI pentest firms and the difficulty of turning bounty style research into a repeatable enterprise sales motion.
notes: Funding unverified: the company website states a $7M seed with Llama Venture, Depth Venture, Y Combinator and over 40 others, but no independent source was found, so no round is recorded. Founder titles differ between the YC profile and launch post. Traction claims (CVEs, bounties) are self reported and the bounty figure differs between pages ($400K vs $580K). The search results mixed in Nebulock, a different company. XBOW funding figures conflict between outlets.
